x: To show that it was now our turn to have a run of good fortune, Peter Morris joined us first claim. Peter was with us in Germany during our tour a couple of years ago and as he was living in London for an extended stay decided to renew his acquaintance with us.

For the last leg we had a new member from Blackpool, Peter Morris, who has an excellent reputation and his first outing for Belgrave was most successful for he not only gained half a minute on Coventry but clinched second place by increasing our lead over Tipton to 24 seconds - an excellent effort w…
New member, Peter Morris, has already done 14.30 and with Adrian Major, Tony Fairclough, Laurie O'Hara, John Bicourt and Lionel Mann backing up, we should have no problems.

Our only winner was Peter Morris with an impressively relaxed performance in the steeplechase. A last element of comedy (peculiar sense of humour!) was provided by the sprint relay being held in a hail storm.

Another impressive performance came in the steeplechase where Peter Morris moved smoothly to a personal best ahead of Dick Piotrowski. Lionel Mann ran his obligatory second race of the day and showed the most unorthodox jump technique since the balmy days of Arkle.
All was not lost though, and with our team being led by Peter Morris, not so overawed by the 'terrors' of road running as some of our track men, we still had a chance.
After very few of the 12 ¾ laps had gone by, the field had split up and the leaders moved steadily away, with Peter Morris leading the procession.

After eight months in the wilderness, Bob Smith came back with a bang on a sultry August evening to collect his first Club Championship trophy (Tom Carter Cup) and really shake Pete Morris and Tony Fairclough.

Our strongest representation was in the 3,000 metres steeplechase where we had John Bicourt Peter Morris and Dick Piotrowski. The latter two just failed to qualify for the final (Peter by the proverbial whisker) and clocked 8:59.0 and 9:03.8 respectively.
Peter Morris, with Bob and Kelly, makes up a trio that were not on call last Autumn and this should produce a terrific battle for selection when the National six-stage relay is due.
John Bicourt continued his steady improvement and it was encouraging to see Peter Morris and Dick Piotrowski (despite a nasty mid-season injury) not far behind.

In addition, new stage records were set by Bill Kerr, Gerry North and Peter Morris. The short season was rounded off with what should have been it's major event---the inaugural 6-stage National Relay at the Crystal Palace.
Peter Morris was not in the least concerned about giving a start to Mullholland of Hercules and it was not long before he was running at the opposition's shoulder.

Some great running by Trevor Hart and Peter Morris took us to within a few seconds of the leaders at the end of stage 8 but some of the opposition was just too strong for Lionel Mann and he finally handed over to Bill Dance with a 45 sec dificit.

It is with many regrets that we say au revoir to PETER MORRIS who, after 6 months with us, has returned to his native Blackpool. If running was the only thing in life then Peter tells me he would have no hesitation in remaining down South, but personal and business committments oblige him to make the move.

With Peter Morris (the holder) back home in Blackpool, and last year's silver medallist Fairclough still on the way to fitness, this year's event was certain to produce a different result if nothing else.
